ModelSurgeon evaluates structural edits with deterministic evidence. A baseline and a
candidate must see the same text, the same tokenizer metadata, the same context window,
and the same batching parameters. The evaluator records the exact model files, tool
revision, command line, and bounded logs so a failed experiment remains diagnosable.

Physical model surgery changes tensor shapes or encoded values while preserving the
surrounding checkpoint contract. A useful benchmark therefore checks more than file
creation. The runtime must load the generated GGUF, tokenize a content-addressed sample,
execute its forward passes, and return a finite perplexity estimate. Comparisons are
rejected when tokenizer metadata differs, because a numerical delta would no longer
describe only the model mutation.

This small public sample is intentionally stable and contains no downloaded benchmark
material. It supports smoke and integration evidence; larger research campaigns should
use a separately pinned dataset revision and publish the corresponding manifest digest.
Raw standard output and standard error remain part of every result, including timeouts,
non-zero exits, truncated logs, and output that cannot be parsed.

Reproducible measurements also separate configuration from observation. Thread count,
microbatch size, logical batch size, context size, warmup policy, processed chunk count,
and GPU offload layers are configuration. Perplexity, uncertainty, return status, and
captured diagnostics are observations. Keeping those roles distinct makes it possible
to compare experiments without silently accepting configuration drift. It also makes a
same-model control useful: the baseline and candidate estimates should agree when every
input byte and runtime setting is held constant.

The benchmark is deliberately bounded. Input content is verified before execution,
model payloads are hashed with a streaming buffer, GGUF tensor bytes remain memory
mapped, and subprocess logs have an explicit maximum size. A timeout is a recorded
failure rather than a successful metric. A final estimate must be finite and at least
one, and uncertainty must be finite and non-negative. These checks turn a command-line
program into a typed evaluation boundary suitable for downstream experiment reports.

Tokenizer equality is established from the complete tokenizer metadata stored inside
each GGUF. File names or user-supplied labels are not sufficient because two checkpoints
can claim the same family while carrying different vocabulary, merge, normalization, or
special-token settings. Hashing the canonical metadata makes the comparison inexpensive
to review and fail closed. Structural surgery is expected to copy that metadata exactly;
if it does not, perplexity cannot isolate the effect of the changed weights or topology.
